selected.assay: bulk RNA-seq (TruSeq, HiSeq, 50 bp SE) of bilateral dorsal hippocampus, 12-week-old male C57BL/6J mice, collected 1 h after a subthreshold 3-min OLM acquisition (S4.2.5.p1, S4.2.6.p1)
selected.sample_inclusion: OLM-trained mice of the six exercise patterns (n=10 each in GEO); RIN>9 (S4.2.6.p1). The GEO 'HC' samples (0-0-0, no OLM) are not part of the paper's described RNA-seq contrasts.
selected.primary_estimand: Effect of each exercise pattern versus sedentary control on dorsal-hippocampus gene expression during OLM consolidation (1 h post acquisition); focus on 14-0-0 and 14-7-2, the patterns that enable long-term memory (S2.2.p1, S4.2.8.p1)
selected.repeated_measure_unit: none (one sample per mouse, independent groups)
selected.batch: tissue collected over two separate days with equal n per group (S4.2.5.p1) = GEO 'harvest cohort'
selected.paper_method: Cyber-T Bayesian-regularized t-test, each exercise group vs sedentary pairwise, on FPKM (S4.2.8.p1); linear regression models as a secondary check (Fig. S2)
selected.paper_results: Per-group DEG counts are only shown graphically (Fig. 2C/D), not stated in text; intersection of up-regulated genes in 14-0-0 and 14-7-2 = 21 genes incl. Bdnf and Acvr1c (S2.2.p1, Data Table S1); Acvr1c not up in 14-7-0 (S2.2.p1)

decisions.reason: Methods S4.2.8.p1: FPKM from Tuxedo; Cyber-T per pair of groups (exercise vs sedentary, 1 h after acquisition); 'only genes with uncorrected p value < 0.05 were used'. No fold-change rule stated. Five exercise groups listed in S4.2.8.p1. DA.p1 names GSE208615.

decisions.reason: Matrix columns equal metadata title (70/70). The sedentary control is 0-0-0 with OLM (sed_*), because every compared group was sampled 1 h after OLM acquisition (S4.2.8.p1). HC (0-0-0, OLM=No) would confound learning with exercise and is excluded.

File named fpkm; data_processing: 'normalization to FPKM values performed using Tuxedo cuffnorm'; 28% integers (mostly zeros), non-integer values, median 1.46. Paper input is FPKM (S4.2.8.p1). Not counts, so DESeq2/edgeR are not applicable.

Six independent groups (n=10 each) with one sedentary control; the paper compares each exercise pattern to sedentary (S4.2.8.p1). One model with planned contrasts vs SED; levels are not pooled. 14-0-0 and 14-7-2 are primary because they carry the paper's main claim (S2.2.p1).

covariates.name: cohort
covariates.disposition: sensitivity only: balanced harvest day (5/group/day, S4.2.5.p1); not in the paper's model

decisions.reason: Independent animals, one sample each. Harvest cohort is perfectly balanced across groups so it is not confounded with exercise; the paper did not adjust for it, so the primary model omits it and a sensitivity run adds it.

selected.method: limma (limma-trend moderated t on log2(FPKM+1), one model ~ grp, contrasts vs SED)

paper_route.reason: no Cyber-T executor in the repository; limma's empirical-Bayes moderated t is the validated analogue (both shrink per-gene variance toward a prior)

deviations: limma moderated t from one six-group model instead of pairwise Cyber-T (pooled residual variance across groups)
genes filtered to FPKM >= 1 in >= 10 samples (smallest group n) to remove unexpressed genes; paper states no filter

decisions.reason: FPKM is log-scale-compatible after log2(x+1); limma is the policy route for FPKM. Cyber-T itself cannot run here.

selected.deviation_note: Paper rule (uncorrected p < 0.05, no FC cutoff) applied to limma p-values instead of Cyber-T; BH FDR < 0.05 reported as audit.

decisions.reason: S4.2.8.p1: 'only genes with both uncorrected p value < 0.05 were used for analysis'.
One limma model on the six OLM groups; contrasts of each exercise pattern vs sedentary as in S4.2.8.p1.
Same model adjusted for the balanced harvest day (S4.2.5.p1).
